questions.q: What sound first told the colts that something was happening?
choices: The cry of dogs in the distance
A church bell ringing over the fields
A distant gunshot
Horses galloping along the high road
questions.evidence: what sounded like the cry of dogs

questions.q: What animal were the hunters and dogs chasing?
choices: A hare
A fox
A stag
A badger

questions.q: When the old horse said the dogs "have lost the scent," what did he mean?
choices: They could no longer smell where the hare went
They were too out of breath to keep running
They had lost their way back to the kennels
They could no longer hear the huntsman's horn

questions.q: What happened to the hare in the end?
choices: The dogs caught her near the fence
She escaped safely into the plantation
She hid among the reeds by the brook
A huntsman picked her up and let her go
questions.evidence: the dogs were upon her with their wild cries

questions.q: What sad sight did Black Beauty see by the brook?
choices: Two fine horses were down
The master's house was on fire
The colts were stuck in the mud
A dog had drowned

questions.q: How did Black Beauty's mother feel about men hunting?
choices: She could not see why men liked a sport that hurt men and horses
She thought it was the finest sport and wished the colts could join
She was proud that her own son Rob Roy was the best hunter there
She said hunting was fine as long as only foxes were ever chased
questions.evidence: I never yet could make out why men are so fond of this sport

questions.q: Who was the young man who was badly hurt?
choices: George Gordon, the squire's only son
Old Daniel, who looked after the horses
Dick, the plowboy who threw the stones
Mr. Bond, the farrier from the village
questions.evidence: it was young George Gordon, the squire's only son

questions.q: Why was the black horse Rob Roy shot?
choices: One of his legs was broken
He had bitten a rider
He was too old to be ridden again
He had run off and spoiled the hunt
questions.evidence: one of his legs was broken

questions.q: What lesson does the last line of the chapter suggest?
choices: A young man and a good horse were lost just to catch one little hare
Hunting is a safe sport as long as riders take care at the brooks
Horses should never be ridden over brooks or high hedges at all
A good hunting dog is worth far more than a horse or a hare
